title: WhatsApp two-step verification codes are ditching six-digit PINs for full passwords
author: Ben Schoon
content:
![](https://9to5google.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2026/08/whatsapp-security-updates.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=1600) 
WhatsApp is making some security upgrades, including turning two-step verification codes into full passwords instead of the traditional six-digit numerical PIN.
Alongside celebrating that one billion of its users are now using passkeys, WhatsApp has two new account security features rolling out.
The first is an upgrade to two-step verification codes used with WhatsApp.
No longer are these codes just a six-digit numerical PIN, but a full password. WhatsApp says these will be “longer, alphanumeric,” and include special characters (@,$, etc) to make the password harder to guess. w
Two-step verification is getting stronger: Two-step verification is an extra protection layer that helps prevent someone from taking over your account, even if they get hold of your one-time passcode. Until now it was a six-digit PIN, we’ve now upgraded it to a full password: longer, alphanumeric, and even with special ch@racters to make it harder to guess. If you’ve been using “123456,” this is your sign to upgrade.
On Android, WhatsApp is also rolling out a new screen for calls that are coming from unknown callers, with the incoming call screen now showing context such as country of origin and whether or not the number is in any of the groups you’re in.
More on WhatsApp:
- WhatsApp updates group chats with new features including ‘@all’ tag
- WhatsApp launches web calling alongside new features: call transfer, waiting room
- Android Auto rolling out upgraded WhatsApp support
Follow Ben: Twitter/X, Threads, Bluesky, and Instagram

![Add 9to5Google as a preferred source on Google](https://9to5google.com/wp-content/themes/ninetofive/dist/images/google-preferred-source-badge-light.png)
summary: WhatsApp is upgrading its two-step verification security feature by replacing the traditional six-digit numerical PIN with longer, alphanumeric passwords that support special characters. Additionally, the platform is rolling out a new incoming call screen for Android users that displays context about unknown callers, such as their country of origin and shared group memberships. These updates are part of broader account security enhancements announced alongside the milestone of one billion passkey users.
key_points: WhatsApp is replacing six-digit numerical PINs with full passwords for two-step verification.
The new passwords will be longer, alphanumeric, and include special characters to improve security.
Android users are receiving a new incoming call screen that provides context for calls from unknown numbers.
WhatsApp recently celebrated reaching one billion passkey users.

title: Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026 report - all the news and announcements as Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past shown for first time
author: Robert Purchese
content:
German mega-show Gamescom officially gets under way this evening with the Opening Night Live showcase hosted by Geoff "bright trainers" Keighley. And we'll be covering all of the news and announcements live, right here, in this article.
The main show begins at 7pm BST (8pm CEST / 2pm EDT / 11am PDT), with a pre-show starting half-an-hour earlier. It's expected to end by 9pm BST so the main show runs for roughly two hours.
What to expect? The big one for me is a first proper look at The Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past, because we barely know anything about it yet. We know it's featuring in Opening Night Live and this glimpse should clarify what the setting is and what new features we can expect.
Elsewhere, I'm excited to see footage of Dungeons & Dragons third-person action game Warlock, because we've only seen a CGI teaser until now, and we know we're going to get a look at the third and final Final Fantasy 7 remake instalment Revelation. Might we also see something more of the new Alien: Isolation 2 game? And I wonder if ArenaNet might show us Guild Wars 3. And could Blizzard announce Diablo 4 on Switch 2?
Besides reveals, we're expecting a flurry of release dates. We still don't have a date for The Duskbloods, which is still set to be out this year, nor the Zelda Ocarina of Time remake, though it'd be a surprise to see a big Nintendo announcement like that here. Much to hope for but what will we get?
![Cover image for YouTube video](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/Zzvzt3IjNik/hqdefault.jpg) gamescom Opening Night Live 2026

- Dungeons & Dragons game Warlock gets a first proper trailer, showing single-player action gameplay
- The Witcher 4's 2028 release date sparks PS5 physical release concerns, but is there anything CD Projekt Red can do to avoid Sony's decision?

summary: The Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026 showcase kicks off in Germany, hosted by Geoff Keighley with a roughly two-hour main show. The event promises major reveals and trailers, including the first proper look at The Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past. Attendees and viewers can also expect gameplay footage for titles like the Dungeons & Dragons action game Warlock and the final Final Fantasy 7 remake instalment Revelation, alongside various release date announcements.
key_points: Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026 runs as a two-hour showcase starting at 7pm BST.
The event features the first proper look at The Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past.
Footage for the Dungeons & Dragons third-person action game Warlock is scheduled to appear.
The showcase is expected to deliver a flurry of new game release dates.

title: Xiaomi 18 Fold is officially coming in September with the monstrous Xring O3 chipset
author: Vlad
content:
The next foldable smartphone from Xiaomi is not going to be called Xiaomi Mix Fold 5, but Xiaomi 18 Fold. The company has officially confirmed this. The device is going to be unveiled in September. It will be the first to use Xiaomi's new Xring O3 chipset, the successor to the Xring O1 from last year.
The Xring O3 managed to score 5,228,014 points in the AnTuTu V11 benchmark. That's more than any other smartphone SoC today.
The SoC features a deca-core CPU with two C1-Ultra cores clocked at up to 4.35GHz, four C1-Premium cores clocked at up to 3.68GHz, and four C1-Pro cores clocked at up to 3.15GHz.
In Geekbench 6.5, it manages a 3,945 single-core score and a 15,221 multi-core score. The Apple A19 Pro still does better in single-core, but is nowhere near the Xring O3 in multi-core.
In select benchmarks, the GPU has managed to be 85%, 94%, and 182% better than the Xring O1's, respectively. It also beats the Apple A19 Pro in all three tests that Xiaomi has shared (you can see them below). The Xring O3 supports LPDDR6 RAM with 113.8GB/s bandwidth.
All in all, it seems like Xiaomi's self-developed chipset has really grown up and will be a serious competitor to the best that Qualcomm, MediaTek, and Apple have to offer.
Shock horror, horror shock Well actually not,not, not & not. First we have ANOTHER 10 core architecture totally different to the 10 core architecture Xiaomi DIDN'T copy from Samsung, indeed their first outing showed us the dynamic...
summary: Xiaomi has officially confirmed that its next foldable smartphone will be named the Xiaomi 18 Fold and will launch in September. It will be the first device to feature the new Xring O3 chipset, a powerful deca-core processor developed by Xiaomi. Benchmark results indicate that the Xring O3 offers exceptional multi-core CPU and GPU performance, positioning it as a major competitor to top processors from Apple, Qualcomm, and MediaTek.
key_points: The upcoming foldable phone will be officially called the Xiaomi 18 Fold.
The device is scheduled to be unveiled in September.
It will debut Xiaomi's new Xring O3 deca-core chipset.
The Xring O3 supports LPDDR6 RAM with 113.8GB/s bandwidth.
The chipset's GPU outperforms the Apple A19 Pro in tests shared by Xiaomi.

title: iPhone 18 Pro launches soon: From price to release date, here’s everything to know
author: Alex Lee
content:
Apple’s big September spectacle is creeping ever closer, and with it, the long-awaited launch of the tech giant’s iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. But will it be a big upgrade, or will the iPhone Ultra steal the show?
Expected to feature the best camera yet, many insiders are predicting the iPhone 18 Pro to feature a DSLR-like variable aperture, giving you precise, manual control over the background blur in your shots. But with the RAM crisis in full effect, you may have to cough up more for the latest flagship than you would have in previous years.
With Apple reportedly punting the release of the regular iPhone 18 to next year, all eyes are currently on the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and the long-rumoured iPhone Ultra. Here's everything we know so far.
Read more: Best refurbished iPhone deals
Latest iPhone 18 Pro news and rumours
Reliable Apple leaker Mark Gurman has reported that the tech giant is preparing a price hike for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max thanks to the ever-increasing costs of components pushing up smartphone prices.
In January, Samsung increased the price of the Galaxy S26 Ultra in the UK, with the entry-level 256GB model increasing by £30 from £1,249 to £1,279. The 512GB model received a much steeper £100 increase, increasing from £1,349 to £1,449.
And earlier this month, Google launched the Pixel 11 Pro for £1,079 and the Pixel 11 Pro XL for £1,279, with both models receiving an £80 price increase over their predecessors.
A couple of months ago, Apple hiked the price of almost every device in its line-up barring the iPhones, including its MacBooks and iPads, so a price increase is likely due.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro release date
The release timeline for the iPhone 18 and subsequent iPhones could look a lot different going forward. In late 2025, the ever-reliable Apple insider Mark Gurman claimed that the company will be moving away from its annual autumnal launch extravaganza. Instead, Gurman claimed it will be spreading its iPhone launches throughout the year.
According to Gurman, the reason for the shift is that Apple’s decision to cram everything into September has become burdensome. It gives the company fewer opportunities to spread out revenue across the year, while also straining its marketing and engineering teams and overloading suppliers.
So Apple’s predicted to shake up its launch window entirely. Gurman says we won’t be seeing the regular iPhone 18 unveiled in September this year. Instead, Apple will only launch the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, as well as its first foldable phone.
The tech giant is then predicted to launch the regular iPhone 18 in the spring of 2027, alongside the iPhone 18e. There’s precedent for this – we’ve just seen Apple launch the iPhone 17e in March, for example. Gurman says the brand could also launch a follow-up to the iPhone Air.
As for the actual release date of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, that’s still fairly easy to predict, given that the date of Apple’s September spectacle isn’t expected to change.
Apple almost always announces its new line of smartphones in the second week of September. To give you an idea, the iPhone 17 was announced on Tuesday 9 September 2025, the iPhone 16 was announced on Monday 9 September 2024, the iPhone 15 on Tuesday 5 September 2023, the iPhone 14 on Wednesday 7 September 2022 and the iPhone 13 on Tuesday 14 September 2021.
Labor Day in the US is on Monday 7 September this year, so Apple is unlikely to unveil its latest launches then. I’m expecting Apple to show off the iPhone 18 Pro on either Tuesday 8 September or Wednesday 9 September – most likely the latter, with pre-orders going live on Friday 11 September. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported in late June that he also believed the iPhone 18 Pro would be unveiled on one of those dates.
The iPhone 18 Pro could then be released on Friday 18 September. However, it might be tricky to acquire if the latest rumours are to be believed.
Former Bloomberg reporter Tim Culpan claims that Apple and its suppliers are scrambling to procure enough memory chips for its upcoming iPhones.
Culpan says that “assemblers are working with Apple to rush shipments of DRAM used in mobile devices”, adding that Apple relies heavily on chip manufacturer Micron for DRAM, but also procures from SK Hynix and Samsung.
That could mean the iPhone 18 Pro will be in even shorter supply than normal when it launches in September, especially if the tech giant isn’t able to manufacture as many smartphones as it would like. A month out and production should ordinarily be full steam ahead by now, with Apple building up stock ahead of one of its biggest launches of the year.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro price
While I always take price increases with a grain of salt, when it comes from Tim Cook himself, it’s no longer just a rumour.
On 17 June, in an interview with The Wall Street Journal, Cook warned that a price hike would be unavoidable. “We're doing our best to mitigate the huge increases that are being passed to us, and we've been trying to shield our customers from the increases, but the situation has become unsustainable,” he said.
A week later, Apple raised prices of the iPad, MacBook, HomePod and Apple TV in the UK. Apple’s entire range of iPads increased by up to £200, the MacBook by up to £300, the HomePod by up to £50 and the Apple TV 4K by up to £100. It’s not a good sign for the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, which are both expected to house even more RAM to power Apple Intelligence
Analysts are now predicting a price hike for the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. A recent Financial Times report is claiming that Apple is racing to secure more RAM from two Chinese chip manufacturers – ChangXin Memory Technologies and Yangtze Memory Technologies. The report claims Apple is lobbying the US government to allow the company to buy the chips from the two state-backed companies, who are blacklisted by the Pentagon, with the Chinese-made phones potentially being limited to China.
However, it may be too late to help lower the cost of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, according to Apple analysts Ming-Chi Kuo, the DRAM shortage will continue to widen into 2027.
Samsung notably increased the price of the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra earlier this year by £30. Apple’s price hike could be even steeper. Analytics firm IDC expects Apple to increase the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max by $100 in the US. Given devices in the UK received the same nominal increase as the US last week, that would translate to a £100 price hike.
The iPhone 17 Pro cost £1,099 at launch, while the iPhone 17 Pro Max launched for £1,199.
This contrasts with what analysts have been saying all year, however, with analysts previously suggesting Apple will absorb any extra costs. Jeff Pu of GF Securities previously stated that the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will cost the same as the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max. In a February 2026 research note obtained by MacRumours, Pu said Apple was looking at keeping the prices the same or similar by focusing on “cost management”.
In the research note, Pu said Apple had been negotiating with Samsung and SK Hynix to achieve relatively “favourable” memory chip deals, and was looking to lower the costs of other parts, such as the camera and display.
The pricing prediction was first raised by the ever-reliable Apple analyst Ming-Chi Kuo, who said in January that Apple was looking to keep the price of the iPhone 18 Pro the same as the previous generation.
On 12 May, MacRumors published a report claiming that Pu expected Apple to outperform in the smartphone market with an “aggressive pricing strategy” for the iPhone 18 Pro. Pu previously predicted that the starting prices of the iPhone 18 Pro models would either remain unchanged from the iPhone 17 Pro lineup or only increase slightly.
That prediction has seemingly changed in recent weeks. The latest report from Pu has poured a bucket of ice-cold water on any hopes of an affordable iPhone this September.
He now reports that the iPhone 18 Pro could come with a $250-$300 price hike, which translates to roughly £185-£220 in the UK. If true, that could mean the iPhone 18 Pro starts from £1,299, making it the most expensive iPhone Pro ever.
Pu claims this is due to the rising cost of 2nm silicon and DRAM/NAND, with Apple passing those costs on to consumers.
In late July, it was revealed that Apple is reportedly racing to secure cheaper components in a bid to offset the price of RAM, which could help keep down the cost of the next iPhone. Korean-based outlet The Elec reported that Apple is pushing Samsung Display and LG Display to supply its OLED panels for $70 each, but that it could get it even lower than that.
The Elec says Apple may get its new OLED panels for just $66.50, which would be a 20 percent reduction compared to the price paid for the iPhone 17 Pro Max.
While The Elec says that the cost of displays has gone down every year, the reduction Apple is seeking is unusually steep. By bringing down the cost of other components, Apple might be able to produce its next iPhone more cheaply, meaning the price hike to you could also be less.
Apple iPhone 18 design and display
While the iPhone 17 Pro looked dramatically different to the iPhone 16 Pro, leakers right now are predicting the iPhone 18 Pro will look fairly similar to the iPhone 17 Pro. The biggest design change is that the Dynamic Island will be shrunk slightly, so that it doesn’t take up as much screen real estate.
In January this year, leaker Ice Universe claimed the Dynamic Island will be 35 per cent narrower than the current version, with a width of around 13.5mm, down from 20.7mm. The leaker shared a mock-up of what that could look like. Ice Universe’s track record has been fairly good for Samsung leaks, but a bit mixed when it comes to Apple.
Earlier rumours suggested Apple was testing a smaller hole-punch cutout instead of a Dynamic Island, with Face ID moving under the screen. This would give the iPhone a screen without interruptions for the first time. However, in January 2026, Weibo leaker Instant Digital stated this had been a mistranslation, and that there would be no hole-punch cutout instead of a Dynamic Island or under-the-screen Face ID.
Instead, the Face ID flood illuminator is the only component that will be moved under the screen, because it’s relatively small. Display industry analyst Ross Young claims Apple will keep this smaller Dynamic Island until at least 2027.
Several leakers have since backed up Ice Universe’s claim. In late March, X account Early Apple shared a supposed prototype image of the iPhone 18 Pro with a shrunken Dynamic Island. The camera flash also appears to illuminate a faint circular area on the display, hinting at the Face ID flood illuminator being hidden under the screen.
Ice Universe also claimed in late March that the bezels on the iPhone 18 series will remain the same as the iPhone 17 and iPhone 16, while reiterating that the Dynamic Island will be smaller.
Another interesting rumour from Instant Digital is that the iPhone 18 Pro Max could be slightly thicker than the iPhone 17 Pro Max, and could weigh roughly 243g. If true, it would make it the heaviest iPhone Apple’s ever produced. That’s 10g heavier than the iPhone 17 Pro Max and 3g heavier than the iPhone 14 Pro Max (the current heavyweight record holder).
Other than that, the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max could look similar to the previous models, boasting 6.3in and 6.9in displays as well as a triple-lens system with the plateau design introduced on the iPhone 17 Pro.
On 22 April, tech YouTuber Vadim Yuryev shared images of dummy units of the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro Max. And if accurate, it doesn’t look like it’s going to be very different to the iPhone 17 Pro Max. But look a little harder, and you’ll notice that the cameras are a lot thicker, with Yuryev stating the black glass on the cameras protrudes a lot more too.
Why is this? According to long-held rumours, the camera is going to get a massive upgrade in September, with Apple implementing variable aperture for the first time and improved sensors.
The first iPhone 18 Pro dummy unit surfaced in late May and early June, giving us a better look at the dark cherry iPhone colourway. While these are just dummy units, they line up with the predicted colour scheme, and come courtesy of TechDroider Clips on YouTube and a Weibo leaker.
In early May, South Korean publication The Elec reported that the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max could boast advanced LTPO+ OLED panels supplied by Samsung Display and LG Display. The upgraded screens are said to be more power efficient, which could help boost battery life, while also being less susceptible to burn-in.
On 29 June, Reuters revealed that more than 200,000 files stolen from Apple's manufacturing partner Tata Electronics had been leaked on the dark web. The leaked archive included supplier lists, engineering documents, component specifications and photos and videos showing the unreleased iPhone 18 Pro undergoing drop testing. It could be the biggest Apple supply chain breach to date.
Cybersecurity researchers say the stolen data began appearing on the dark web on 10 June, but Tata Electronics hadn’t reported the data breach until 22 June. In the leaked videos and images, a drop test of a smartphone with a three-camera layout and Apple logo can be seen. Last week, AppleInsider reported that board layouts for the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max were also contained in the data breach, as well as a data sheet for the upcoming A18 Pro chip.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro colours
One interesting decision Apple made for the iPhone 17 Pro was to give the handsets a two-tone design. Controversially, the glass back for MagSafe charging is a different colour to the aluminium frame, making it look less uniform. Apple is reportedly looking to reduce this contrast for the iPhone 18 Pro.
In November 2025, Instant Digital reported that Apple had changed the phone’s back glass process to help minimise the two-tone look seen on the iPhone 17 Pro, giving the phones a more unified look.
![](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/04/16/9/18/iphone-18-deep-red.png)
In late February, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman also claimed that Apple was testing a deep red colour for the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Fold. On 11 April, Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station claimed the same, based on the fact the insider has seen prototypes of Android phones in the same deep red colour.
On 1 May, Macworld claimed a source familiar with Apple’s supply chain had information regarding the colourways for the upcoming smartphones. According to the publication, the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will come in a dark cherry colourway, which it says will be “much closer to wine than fruit punch”. It says that Apple has also been experimenting with a light blue colourway, similar to the iPhone 17’s mist blue, as well as a dark grey. There will also reportedly be a silver colourway to complete the line-up.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro cameras
Of all the features to receive the biggest shake-up, it’s almost always the camera system
In December 2024, Ming-Chi Kuo claimed the main rear camera on the iPhone 18 Pro will feature variable aperture for the first time, making it act more like a DSLR camera. Variable aperture would enable iPhone users to control how much light comes through the lens. Kuo claimed Dutch manufacturer BE Semiconductor would supply the assembly equipment used to produce the aperture blades.
Several reputable leakers have since corroborated this leak in recent months, with ETNews the latest to do so, in October 2025. The iPhones have had fixed apertures for years, so this could be a significant upgrade.
Apple is also reportedly testing a new telephoto camera for the iPhone 18 Pro. Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station claimed in October last year that the telephoto lens will also feature a larger aperture, being upgraded from the iPhone 17 Pro’s f/2.8 telephoto lens.
Another (fairly old) leak, from January 2025, comes from Taiwanese publication DigiTimes. The publication claimed that Samsung has developed a new three-layer stacked camera sensor system specifically for the iPhone 18. According to DigiTimes, this would make the iPhone 18’s cameras more responsive and reduce noise.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro specs
Spec details for the iPhone 18 Pro are still fairly thin on the ground, but several leaks suggest Apple’s next-generation A20 chip will power the devices.
According to Jeff Pu, the A20 chip is expected to use TSMC’s new 2nm manufacturing process, which could make it up to 15 per cent faster and 30 per cent more efficient than the current A19 chip.
An August 2025 report from Ming-Chi Kuo also suggests the A20 could use a new chip packaging method that integrates RAM directly with the processor, potentially improving performance for Apple Intelligence features, while freeing up space inside the phone.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman also claims iPhone 18 Pro models will feature Apple’s next-generation C2 modem. The chip is expected to improve 5G performance and could add support for mmWave connectivity, bringing it closer to the Qualcomm modems Apple currently uses. Weibo leaker Fixed Digital also suggested, in February 2026, that it could support new satellite connectivity standards, potentially allowing for full internet access over satellite networks when traditional coverage isn’t available.
Weibo leaker Fixed Focus Digital has claimed that Apple’s A20 Pro chip could be 18 per cent faster than the A19 Pro, though could be more expensive to manufacture.
According to the leaker, the A20 Pro is rumoured to use TSMC’s new 2nm manufacturing process, with a new transistor design known as GAA. This should mean Apple can squeeze more performance out of the chip without using more power. If true, it should make the phone more efficient, with Fixed Focus Digital claiming it’ll consume up to 30 per cent less power than the A19 Pro.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro battery
In early July, new regulatory certification filings from China were discovered by Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station purporting to show the battery capacity for both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.
According to the filings in China's C3 database, the iPhone 18 Pro Max will have a 4,056mAh battery in China, while the US eSIM-only handset will get a 4,288mAh battery. That’s slightly up on the 3,988mAh and 4,252mAh battery capacity for the iPhone 17 Pro. The iPhone 18 Pro Max will reportedly getting a much bigger battery life boost, however.
The filing says the iPhone 18 Pro Max will boast a 5,391mAh battery in China, with the eSIM-only model in the US getting a 5,567mAh battery. That’s a huge jump on the iPhone 17 Pro Max’s 4,823mAh battery in China and the 5,088mAh battery in the US. In comparison, the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra has a 5,000mAh battery.
I’ll be rounding up all the latest leaks right here on this page as more rumours come in, so stay tuned.
The best iPhone 17 Pro carrier deals
Don’t want to wait months to get your hands on a new iPhone? The iPhone 17 Pro is a splendid phone and, right now, it doesn’t look like the upgrade to the iPhone 18 Pro will be massive. Below, we’ve rounded up some of the best iPhone 17 Pro carrier deals in the UK.
![Apple claims the iPhone 17 Pro Max can last up to 39 hours on a single charge](https://static.independent.co.uk/2025/09/10/15/50/iphone-17-pro-orange.png)
Affordable Mobiles currently has one of the cheapest iPhone 17 Pro deals. You can get the phone with 100GB of data for £49 per month and a £39 up-front cost. The deal is with mobile network Three, meaning you get access to Three+ rewards and free wifi on the London underground.
![If you’ve bought a new iPhone in the last five years, you’re in luck](https://static.independent.co.uk/2025/09/15/8/24/iOS-26-IndyBest.jpg)

For more, we’ve reviewed the latest iPhone 17e to see if it’s worth the price tag
summary: Apple is expected to launch the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max in September, alongside possible changes to its future release schedule. The new models are anticipated to feature a shrunken Dynamic Island, a DSLR-like variable aperture camera, and potentially higher prices due to rising component costs and memory chip shortages. CEO Tim Cook and various industry analysts have warned that price hikes are likely, driven by the increasing costs of RAM and silicon.
key_points: The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are predicted to be unveiled in September, with pre-orders potentially opening on September 11.
A global RAM shortage and increasing component costs are expected to lead to a price increase for the new iPhone Pro models.
The Dynamic Island is rumored to be shrunk by about 35 percent, making it narrower than previous versions.
Apple is reportedly moving the Face ID flood illuminator under the screen while keeping the overall display design similar to the iPhone 17 Pro.

title: Apple Launches The M6 2nm 12-core CPU, Quad-Die M5 Ultra
author: Michael Larabel
content:
Apple Launches The M6 2nm 12-core CPU, Quad-Die M5 Ultra
![APPLE](https://www.phoronix.com/assets/categories/apple.webp)
The Apple M6 base model launched today for the new Mac Mini. The Apple M6 is their first TSMC 2nm chip and features a 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, and dual 16-core neural engine. The M6 supports up to 170GB/s of unified memory bandwidth.
Twelve cores with the M6 is two more than the M5 and is a combination of two super cores, four performance cores, and six efficiency cores. The M6 is said to provide "the world's fastest single-threaded performance" and up to 1.2x the multi-threaded performance of the M5 or now up to 2.4x faster than the original M1.
The M5 Ultra debuted alongside the M6 with being their first quad-die architecture and most powerful Apple Silicon design ever for AI and professional workloads. The M5 Ultra supports up to 36 CPU cores, up to an 80 core GPU, and 1.2TB/s of unified memory bandwidth.
More details on the Apple M6 with the new Mac Mini along with the M5 Ultra debuting in the new Mac Studio can be found via the announcement this morning on Apple.com.
With the launch of the M5 Ultra and M6, yet more work piles up for Asahi Linux and those bringing Apple Silicon support to Linux and the BSDs.With Linux 7.3 they are up to very basic support for the M3 Pro / Max / Ultra for at least booting to a console but not yet any GPU acceleration or other features needed to daily use Apple M3 products on Linux.
summary: Apple has launched the M6 base model chip for the new Mac Mini, featuring a 2nm process, a 12-core CPU, and improved performance. Alongside the M6, Apple introduced the M5 Ultra, its first quad-die architecture chip designed for the new Mac Studio. These new releases continue to present ongoing development challenges for bringing Apple Silicon support to Linux and BSD.
key_points: The Apple M6 is the company's first TSMC 2nm chip, featuring a 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, and dual 16-core neural engine.
The M6 CPU configuration consists of two super cores, four performance cores, and six efficiency cores.
The M5 Ultra debuted as Apple's first quad-die architecture, supporting up to 36 CPU cores and an 80-core GPU.
The M6 launches with the new Mac Mini, while the M5 Ultra debuts in the new Mac Studio.
The new chip launches add to the workload for developers bringing Apple Silicon support to Linux and the BSDs.

title: New Garmin Fenix 9 is built to help you “perform better and venture farther” | BikeRadar
author: Nick Clark
content:
Garmin has updated its flagship outdoor smartwatch with the new Fenix 9 and Fenix 9 Pro bringing brighter displays, faster mapping and new endurance-focused features.
The Fenix 9 gets an AMOLED display that Garmin says is twice as bright as its predecessor, while the Fenix 9 Pro adds a titanium case, a display reaching up to 3,000 nits and optional inReach satellite and LTE connectivity.
Susan Lyman, Garmin Vice President of Consumer Sales and Marketing, says the watches are "purpose-built for those who want to perform better and venture farther."
The watches are aimed squarely at endurance athletes and outdoor adventurers, with features that should appeal to cyclists and runners in particular.
The new smartwatches are available in 43mm, 47mm and 51mm case sizes, with the Fenix 9 starting at £859.99 / $999.99 for the 43mm and 47mm variants and topping out at £949.99 / $1,099 for the 51mm size.
The Fenix 9 Pro and Fenix 9 Pro Solar are priced at £949.99 / $1,099.99 for the 43mm and 47mm, and the 51mm case size costs £1,029.99 / $1,199.99.
Brighter displays and faster maps
![Garmin Fenix 9 Pro display](https://www.bikeradar.com/resources/content/32337f2f-7841-4ef6-a233-d1f001580530/4015f975-d3cd-4d3d-a05a-3feea7f5ddea/ca93a6d6-5e01-4f92-81c9-612d74ff2b19/Garmin-Fenix-9-Pro-display.webp?preview=false&platform=WEB&deviceId=2ab373ab-8d1b-4a03-b345-b6bec973750f)
The Fenix 9's AMOLED display is designed to improve readability in bright conditions, while Garmin has increased the watch's RAM by 50% compared to the Fenix 8.
An updated map engine is claimed to make panning around maps up to 30% faster, with a new perspective view showing more detail both close to the user and further ahead on a route.
Storage has also doubled to 64GB, with Garmin saying this should enable users to download twice as many maps and store up to 7,000 songs.
The watch also introduces Garmin Epic, which allows users to combine multiple activities into a single story in Garmin Connect.
This could be useful for multi-day events, bike tours or training blocks, bringing activities, health data and photos together into what is essentially one activity.
Garmin has also introduced new stamina zones and a stamina curve, designed to show how endurance changes over time and help athletes understand the impact of training and fitness gains.
Titanium case
![Garmin Fenix 9 Pro on Orange Strap](https://www.bikeradar.com/resources/content/32337f2f-7841-4ef6-a233-d1f001580530/4015f975-d3cd-4d3d-a05a-3feea7f5ddea/30908854-178d-46df-993d-ab9e16113c0e/Garmin-Fenix-9-Pro-Orange-Strap.webp?preview=false&platform=WEB&deviceId=2ab373ab-8d1b-4a03-b345-b6bec973750f)
The range-topping Fenix 9 Pro comes with a titanium case, using Garmin's nano-moulding technology to combine metal and plastic.
The Pro's AMOLED display reaches up to 3,000 nits, while the 51mm model gets a 1.5-inch display – Garmin's largest-ever Fenix screen.
The brand says the larger display increases viewing area by 15% without increasing the case size.
Solar-charging versions are available, while the integrated LED flashlight gains a green-light mode intended to preserve night vision.
![Garmin Fenix 9 Pro Emergency Response](https://www.bikeradar.com/resources/content/32337f2f-7841-4ef6-a233-d1f001580530/4015f975-d3cd-4d3d-a05a-3feea7f5ddea/7586df85-5d2d-4604-baec-f07484a39d92/Garmin-Fenix-9-Pro-Emergency-Response.webp?preview=false&platform=WEB&deviceId=2ab373ab-8d1b-4a03-b345-b6bec973750f)
The Pro also introduces built-in inReach connectivity to the Fenix range, with compatible models able to make calls, send messages and trigger SOS alerts without a phone.
For the first time, Garmin is offering inReach-enabled versions across all three Pro case sizes.
The LTE connectivity can also provide location sharing through Garmin Messenger, while satellite connectivity can deliver weather forecasts directly to the watch.
Garmin claims up to 29 days of smartwatch battery life for the largest Fenix 9, while the 51mm Fenix 9 Pro is rated for up to 31 days.
Solar versions can stretch this to as much as 57 days under Garmin's specified conditions.
summary: Garmin has announced the new Fenix 9 and Fenix 9 Pro outdoor smartwatches, tailored for endurance athletes and outdoor adventurers. The updated line features brighter AMOLED displays, faster mapping engines, increased storage, and new endurance-focused tracking tools. Additionally, the Pro models introduce a titanium case, optional LTE and inReach satellite connectivity, and solar-charging capabilities.
key_points: The Fenix 9 features an AMOLED display that is twice as bright as its predecessor, while the Fenix 9 Pro reaches up to 3,000 nits.
Storage has doubled to 64GB, and RAM has increased by 50% to support 30% faster map panning.
The Fenix 9 Pro models introduce built-in inReach satellite and LTE connectivity across all three case sizes.
New endurance features include Garmin Epic for combining multiple activities, stamina zones, and a stamina curve.
Prices for the Fenix 9 start at £859.99 / $999.99, with the Fenix 9 Pro and Pro Solar ranging up to £1,029.99 / $1,199.99 for the 51mm size.

title: Garmin Fenix 9: Eight Key Facts About Garmin’s Latest Watch
author: Andrew Williams
content:
Garmin has announced the Garmin Fenix 9, the latest version of its most well-regarded adventure and running watch series.
The Garmin Fenix 9 series starts at $999.99, and comes in both standard and Pro variants, while in the past the Pro line has been released as a separate generational refresh.
In the usual Garmin fashion, there are absolutely loads of versions — 16 by my count before you even start thinking about finishes — so I’m here to pare the Fenix 9 down to the essentials.
Here are of the top facts you should know about the Fenix 9, which will be available to order from August 28.
3,000-nit Brightness (OLED) But No Garmin Fenix 9 MicroLED
OLED versions of the Garmin Fenix 9 are rated for 3,000-nit screen brightness. While this is nowadays quite a normal figure for a higher-end OLED smartwatch, it’s far higher peak brightness than the Fenix 8 line, rated at up to 1,000 nits.
This year there’s no sign of another microLED model, offered in the Fenix 8 Pro line-up. This could well be down to limited demand for that model, and that its increased bulk and cost just doesn’t justify the brightness bump offered over a 3,000-nit OLED display.
The microLED Fenix 8 Pro can reach up to 4,500 nits. Brighter, but not three times as bright like last time around.
There’s A Solar Charging Version, With A Catch
At one point it looked like Garmin might replace all its MIP watch screens with OLEDs. But the Fenix 9 line shows there is still enough of a market for the old style: the Pro Solar models have MIP screens.
This kind of display gets clearer in bright environments rather than having to compete with them like an OLED panel. And it’s the only display style still compatible with Garmin’s solar charging tech.
The Garmin Fenix 9 Pro Solar is available in 47mm and 51mm sizes and promises the longest battery life of the whole family — at least when exposed to enough direct sunlight. With solar charging, Garmin rates the 47mm version at up to 34 days of use, the 51mm version at up 57 days.
It’s not quite the “up to 90 days” of the Garmin Enduro 3, but it’s not bad at all.
All Versions Have A Part-Titanium Casing
In the Garmin Fenix 8 generation some of the watches used part stainless steel casings. This time around, lighter titanium is the standard, and what varies is how much of Garmin’s “fiber reinforced polymer” is used in each model.
This leads to lower weight, which can help improve comfort and the reliability of heart rate readings.
Garmin Fenix 9 Pro Versions Make More Use Of Titanium
The difference between the standard Fenix 9 and Fenix 9 Pro isn’t immediately obvious. While there’s no huge feature separation between the two if you discount the option on InReach Satellite connectivity, the designs are quite different.
Standard Fenix 9 watches use a mix of titanium and “fiber reinforced polymer.” Most notably the side walls are plastic, while the bezel and the rear plate are metal.
In the Fenix 9 Pro all of the main components are titanium. And this leads to a slight shift in weight across models, with the disparity rising in the larger variants. Here are the numbers for the main watch body only:
- 43mm Fenix 9 - 44g
- 43mm Fenix 9 Pro - 45g
- 47mm Fenix 9 - 53g
- 47mm Fenix 9 Pro - 56g
- 51mm Fenix 9 - 63g
- 51mm Fenix 9 Pro. - 73g
It’s that last pair that brings a weight difference you might start to actually notice, although overall weight will also be steered by the strap. So, yes, some of you might actually prefer the 51mm standard Fenix 9 over the 51mm Fenix 9 Pro.
Full Garmin Fenix 9 Pricing details
Here’s how much you’ll pay for all the key Fenix 9 variants in the U.S..
- Fenix 9 (43mm) - $999.99
- Fenix 9 Pro (43mm) - $1099.99
- Fenix 9 (47mm) - $999.99
- Fenix 9 Pro (47mm) - $1099.99
- Fenix 9 Pro Solar (47mm) - $1099.99
- Fenix 9 (51mm) - $1099.99
- Fenix 9 Pro (51mm) - $1199.99
- Fenix 9 Pro Solar (51mm) - $1199.99
All Pro models are available as an InReach Connectivity satellite version for an extra $100.
Satellite connectivity for Pro Garmin Fenix 9 models only
All Pro variants of the Garmin Fenix 9 are available with and without InReach Satellite connectivity. This requires an additional subscription, starting at $7.99 a month.
It’s used for LTE and satellite communication, for messages without a connected phone, LTE calls and for SOS alerts in remote locations.
InReach, while a great feature, clearly isn’t something everyone wants or needs, so it’s good you get to take it or leave it — at $100 for the hardware upgrade.
Garmin Fenix 9: Double the storage, more RAM
Garmin Fenix 8 watches and other recent high-end Garmins to date have typically had 32GB storage for on-watch maps and music. That jumps to 64GB in the Fenix 9 — more room for more maps, more music. Simple.
Garmin also says RAM has been increased too, although the company never talks at any length about these hardware elements — I expect they wouldn’t compare to what an Apple Watch Ultra uses, for example. Garmin says the additional RAM helps improve map nvaigation speed, which will be a welcome change.
Some software tweaks
There are some minor changes to the Fenix’s software feature line-up, and time will let if these drip down to existing lines.
Garmin Epic lets you corral together a bunch of activities, over “several days, weeks or months” to turn them into a shareable nugget that includes photos, health and performance data. It’s one for those walking holidays and adventure expeditions.
Indoor rowing has been improved too. To use Garmin’s own words, you get additional insights “like VO2 Max and power curve, to evaluate progress, set goals and dial in the intensity of workouts.”
The Garmin Fenix 9 series watches will be available to order from August 28.
summary: Garmin has announced the Fenix 9 adventure and running watch series, available to order starting August 28 with prices beginning at $999.99. The new lineup includes standard, Pro, and Pro Solar variants across 16 different versions featuring brighter OLED displays, titanium construction, and increased storage and RAM. Additionally, Pro models offer optional InReach Satellite connectivity and introduce new software features like Garmin Epic and improved indoor rowing metrics.
key_points: The Garmin Fenix 9 series starts at $999.99 and will be available to order starting August 28.
OLED models feature a peak brightness of 3,000 nits, while Pro Solar models use MIP screens compatible with solar charging.
Storage has doubled to 64GB, and increased RAM helps improve map navigation speed.
All versions feature a part-titanium casing, with Pro models making more extensive use of titanium components.
Pro variants offer optional InReach Satellite connectivity for an additional $100 plus a monthly subscription.

title: Google, take note: This phone maker's new chipset looks like an absolute beast
author: Hadlee Simons
content:
Google, take note: This phone maker's new chipset looks like an absolute beast
Aug 24, 2026 — 6:14 AM ET
- Xiaomi has announced the XRing 03 smartphone chipset.
- This chipset has an unannounced Arm G2-Ultra NX GPU and a 10-core CPU with no little cores.
- The chip will debut in the Xiaomi 18 Fold, which is scheduled to launch next month.
Google has just launched the Pixel 11 series, and our own benchmarks show that the Tensor G6 chip is a significant step down from rival chips. Now, Xiaomi has revealed its XRing 03 processor, and it seemingly obliterates Google’s silicon on paper.
Xiaomi revealed XRing 03 details on Weibo, and it packs a 3nm design from an unspecified foundry. However, what’s particularly interesting is that it comes with an unannounced Arm G2-Ultra NX GPU. Expect 16 cores, eight NX neural accelerators, and AI-based super-resolution/frame interpolation. In fact, Xiaomi claims that this GPU is 85% faster than last year’s XRing 01, 64% more efficient, and 182% faster at ray tracing. For what it’s worth, the XRing 01 had an Immortalis G925 MC16 GPU. Either way, this seems far more impressive than the Tensor G6’s PowerVR CXTP-48-1536 GPU.
The company didn’t reveal the exact CPU cores, but noted that you can expect a decacore layout with six “super” cores, four “large” cores, and a 4.35GHz peak clock speed. Xiaomi says the CPU has “dual” SME2 acceleration units for AI tasks. SME is particularly important for AI workloads that aren’t optimized for the NPU. Otherwise, you should expect 60% faster performance than the XRing 01 and up to 25% lower power consumption. Xiaomi’s previous chipset packed a 10-core CPU consisting of two Cortex-X925 cores, six Cortex-A725 cores, and two Cortex-A520 cores.
Otherwise, Xiaomi says you can expect a four-core NPU with 45% faster local AI performance, 200 TOPS of tensor computing power, and a claimed 3.3 teraflops of vector processing power. We’re not sure how this compares to Google and Qualcomm’s latest chips, but the MediaTek Dimensity 9500 apparently packs an NPU with 100 TOPS of power. So it looks like Xiaomi is bringing a ton of AI horsepower here. You can also expect support for LPDDR6 RAM.
On the multimedia front, the Xiaomi XRing 03 supports a single 432MP camera. This dwarfs MediaTek and Qualcomm’s 320MP single camera capabilities. Then again, we haven’t even seen any 320MP smartphone cameras just yet. However, Xiaomi’s chipset also supports H.266 (VVC) video decoding for higher quality video at a reduced file size. This comes after Android 17 rolled out VVC support as well. You should also expect 4K/60fps capture and noise reduction for night video.
Xiaomi has confirmed that the XRing 03 will debut in its Xiaomi 18 Fold, which is officially scheduled to launch next month. Either way, this tentatively looks like an impressive smartphone processor. We’re not sure about the CPU, but that GPU specs definitely suggest that Xiaomi phones with this chip will easily outperform the Pixel 11 series in games. And you probably won’t run into severe issues running Genshin Impact.
summary: Xiaomi has announced its new XRing 03 smartphone chipset, featuring a powerful 3nm design, an unannounced Arm G2-Ultra NX GPU, and a 10-core CPU with no efficiency cores. The processor boasts significant performance and efficiency improvements over its predecessor, including advanced AI capabilities and support for LPDDR6 RAM. The XRing 03 is scheduled to make its debut next month in the upcoming Xiaomi 18 Fold.
key_points: Xiaomi announced the XRing 03 smartphone chipset, which features a 3nm design.
The chipset includes a 10-core CPU with a peak clock speed of 4.35GHz and no little cores.
The unannounced Arm G2-Ultra NX GPU offers significant performance, efficiency, and ray tracing upgrades.
The XRing 03 supports a single 432MP camera and H.266 video decoding.
The new processor will debut next month in the Xiaomi 18 Fold.

title: Apple's 20th anniversary iPhone could take some inspiration from Android phones
author: Chethan Rao
content:
Apple's 20th anniversary iPhone could take some inspiration from Android phones
Aug 24, 2026 — 2:13 PM ET
![Apple iPhone Air 9 Apple iPhone Air 9](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Apple-iPhone-Air_9-scaled-e1761389770799.jpg)
- Apple may be prepping radical design changes for the 20th anniversary iPhone, according to a new leak.
- The leaked renders show curved glass on the front and back with two horizontally placed cameras at the back.
- We’re also seeing what appears to be a hole-punch selfie camera on the screen, reminiscent of present-day Android phones.
The iPhone is expected to see a radical shakeup this year, with Apple’s first-ever foldable likely to be revealed during the fall event next month. However, the company will reach a bigger milestone in 2027, marking 20 years since the first iPhone was revealed in 2007. A new leak is giving us our first potential look at the next-gen iPhone model Apple could introduce to celebrate.
Leaker Yogesh Brar shares a couple of images on X that appear to show the 20th anniversary iPhone from multiple angles, including a clear view of its sides. It also appears to show a quad curved display on the front and a similarly curved glass on the rear panel. The images reveal dual rear cameras positioned horizontally, rather than vertically as on the iPhone 17. But for as interesting as all that is, it’s also hard to ignore some of the discrepancies in this particular leak.
![20th anniversary iphone yb 2 20th anniversary iphone yb 2](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20th-anniversary-iphone-yb-2.jpeg)
The image above, seemingly depicting the front and back profiles of the 20th anniversary iPhone model, appears to be missing the Camera Control button, which is typically placed on the right side of the iPhone, sitting some distance below the power button.
![20th anniversary iphone yb 3 20th anniversary iphone yb 3](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20th-anniversary-iphone-yb-3.jpeg)
Meanwhile, the second set of supposed 20th anniversary iPhone renders shows a randomly placed key on the left-hand side of the device, with no volume rocker or the Action button visible. These mismatches might suggest that some form of generative AI tool was used to make these images, potentially using a simple description from supply chain sources, though we cannot independently confirm this.
Another notable aspect of these leaked images is the front camera. Per these images, Apple may ditch the Dynamic Island altogether and use a more conventional hole-punch front camera instead. It’s unclear where the sensors for Apple’s Face ID tech will be positioned, however.
Given how essential Dynamic Island is for the iPhone, we would be surprised if Apple took this step. However, if the company does go in that direction and adopts a hole-punch selfie camera, it would be borrowing a common design attribute from Android phones.
Given some of the inconsistencies we mentioned above, we’d recommend taking this leak with a grain of salt. Hopefully, we’ll get a better idea of the 20th anniversary iPhone model as we head into 2027. For now, Apple’s focus will be firmly on next month’s iPhone 18 launch event, which should also play host to the iPhone Ultra foldable.
Reports say Apple may skip the iPhone 19 altogether and jump straight to the iPhone 20 (XX) next year. This wouldn’t be a first for the company, given that it released the iPhone X in 2017 to mark the 10th anniversary of iPhones, alongside the iPhone 8 and 8 Plus.
summary: A recent leak suggests Apple's 20th anniversary iPhone in 2027 could feature radical design changes, including curved glass and a hole-punch selfie camera similar to Android phones. The leaked renders show inconsistencies like missing or misplaced physical buttons, indicating the images may have been generated using AI based on supply chain descriptions. Observers recommend taking the leak with skepticism as Apple prepares for its upcoming fall events.
key_points: A new leak reveals potential renders of Apple's 20th anniversary iPhone.
The leaked design features curved glass on both the front and back, alongside a hole-punch selfie camera.
Inconsistencies with physical buttons suggest the images may have been created using generative AI.
Adopting a hole-punch camera would mean Apple might ditch the Dynamic Island, mirroring a common Android design.

title: iPhone 18 Pro Leaks Are Everywhere. Which Ones Can You Actually Trust?
author: Jibin Joseph
content:
![](https://sm.pcmag.com/t/pcmag_uk/news/i/iphone-18-/iphone-18-pro-leaks-are-everywhere-which-ones-can-you-actual_v8rp.1920.jpg) (Credit: PCMag/Apple)
If you're not ready to try out a foldable, Apple's next iPhone event is also likely to include the launch of the iPhone 18 Pros.
Customers usually hold off on iPhone purchases right before Apple’s fall event, but the RAM crisis and its associated price hikes may have you wondering whether it's best to buy now and avoid any more increases. Apple already raised prices across several major product lines in June, but the iPhone was not included, helping drive iPhone 17 sales during the last quarter.
To make your decision easier, we’ve rounded up the biggest iPhone 18 Pro rumors we have heard so far. While these features and prices aren’t confirmed yet, they should help paint a picture of what to expect from Apple’s next big smartphones.
iPhone 18 Pro: Revised Lineup
The biggest rumor around the iPhone 18 lineup is its release timeline. Unlike previous years, where Apple released four phones in the same series in one go, Bloomberg reports Apple could take a two-pronged approach to ensure consistent revenue throughout the year.
Flagship phones, such as the iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, and the first-ever foldable iPhone, could be unveiled in September, while the base iPhone 18, iPhone Air 2, and the iPhone 18e could be launched in spring 2027. We discuss the foldable iPhone in detail in a separate rumor round-up, so we’ll just stick to the Pro models here.
iPhone 18 Pro: Design and Colors
The iPhone 17 Pro models brought a major overhaul to Apple’s smartphone design language, with a new camera “plateau” and two-toned color scheme. This year, Apple isn’t expected to drastically change the device's appearance, but it could add a few bold colors and return to a more uniform color scheme on the back.
Several leakers, including Sonny Dickson and Instant Digital, claim that Apple could go with a never-before-seen cherry red and a new light blue, alongside the regular dark gray. Dickson also shared pictures of potential dummies, including one in light gray.
While the appearance of the rear is expected to remain the same, the in-hand feel could be a lot different. Ice Universe says the battery could get slightly larger on the iPhone 18 Pro Max, contributing to increased weight and bulk. More precisely, the leaker expects the device to be 0.25mm thicker and 7 grams heavier.
iPhone 18 Pro Display
On the front, we might see one significant change. The Dynamic Island, or the camera cutout, could be reduced by 35%, Ice Universe says. This won’t shrink the feature's overall functionality, but it could move the Face ID sensor’s illuminator to one corner below the screen.
When it comes to display sizes, the consensus is that the iPhone 18 Pro will come in its usual 6.3-inch screen, while the Pro Max will have a 6.9-inch screen. Apple, however, has reportedly been pushing suppliers to provide much brighter displays and could use the more power-efficient LTPO+ display tech.
iPhone 18 Pro Cameras
The iPhone 17 Pro lineup bumped all three cameras to 48MP. For the iPhone 18 Pro, the biggest camera-related rumor we have heard is around variable aperture. While the iPhone 17 models had a fixed aperture, the iPhone 18 Pro may introduce a variable aperture. ETNews reports that the modified system has already entered production and would help the cameras deliver more light to the sensors in dark conditions and reduce light in bright conditions.
Apple may also modify its relatively new Camera Control button. Introduced with the iPhone 16, the capacitive button at the bottom right of the phone lets you quickly launch the Camera app, take pictures, and adjust settings for zoom, exposure, depth, and other controls. Mastering the capacitive button, however, has proved difficult, with users noting that they have been accidentally launching the Camera app. Apple may finally fix the problem by removing the touch-sensitive components of the button and delivering a more user-friendly experience, 9to5Mac reports.
iPhone 18 Pro Performance
The iPhone 18 Pro is likely to receive a performance boost with the A20 chip. It will use TSMC’s 2nm technology, an upgrade from the previous generation’s 3nm tech. The transition will allow more transistors on each chip but also raise chip costs by 50%, MacRumors reports.
The chip is also rumored to have TSMC’s Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module (WMCM) technology, which infuses RAM into the same wafer as the CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine. Overall, it is expected to be 18% faster and 30% more power-efficient than previous generations, according to leaker Fixed Focus Digital.
Apple usually reserves the base variant of its chip series for the standard iPhone models, while the Pro models get the corresponding Pro chip. With the iPhone 18 series, Apple is reportedly considering offering just the high-end variant across the lineup.
Another expected upgrade is for the modem. The iPhone 17 Pro models had an unspecified third-party modem, but the iPhone 18 Pro could get the company’s proprietary C2 modem. It will support 5G satellite connectivity and reduce the scope of location data retained by networks, according to MacRumors.
iPhone 18 Pro Battery
Apple never reveals its battery capacities, but multiple leakers have indicated a larger and more efficient battery for the iPhone 18 Pro Max. According to Digital Chat Station, the top variant will have a capacity of up to 5,200mAh, slightly better than the 5,088mAh capacity of its predecessor. With a more efficient modem and processor, the battery life could be significantly longer. The iPhone 18 Pro, on the other hand, could see a minimal bump from 4,252mAh to 4,288mAh.
More recently, leaks posted on Korean and Chinese social media sites tip a US iPhone 18 Pro Max model with a 5,567mAh battery, a nearly 10% increase over the iPhone 17 Pro Max, MacRumors notes.
iPhone 18 Pro: Pricing and Release
This is what much of the decision-making hinges on. Apple has avoided raising prices for its biggest revenue generator, but rising RAM and storage costs are unavoidable, by outgoing CEO Tim Cook’s own admission.
Common sense suggests a price hike for iPhones is inevitable in September. According to The Wall Street Journal's estimate, rising component costs would push the iPhone 18 Pro to start at $1,299. If you couple that with recent Apple trends, the iPhone 18 Pro Max could be priced $100 higher, taking its starting price to $1,399. In comparison, the iPhone 17 Pro starts at $1,099, while the 17 Pro Max starts at $1,199.
When asked on a recent earnings call about potential price hikes for the iPhone, Cook said it's "too early to come to a definitive conclusion of what happens there. Because it takes a little while for the channels to adjust since there's channel inventory, it takes a while for the consumer to respond. We'll understand that more in the weeks ahead."
The iPhone 18 Pro’s release date hasn’t been finalized yet. Going by previous event dates, Sept. 9, 2026, probably makes the most sense for the announcement, with a ship date the following week, but we'll have to wait for those invitations to hit our inboxes to know for sure.
summary: Apple's upcoming iPhone 18 Pro lineup faces widespread rumors regarding a split release schedule, potential design tweaks, and performance upgrades. Key speculation points to a new A20 chip, variable aperture cameras, and a proprietary C2 modem, alongside anticipated price increases driven by rising component costs. While these details remain unconfirmed, they offer a preview of what consumers might expect from Apple's next flagship smartphones.
key_points: Apple may split its release timeline, launching flagship models like the iPhone 18 Pro in September and base models in the spring.
The iPhone 18 Pro lineup is rumored to feature a variable aperture camera system and a reduced Dynamic Island.
Performance is expected to improve with a 2nm A20 chip and a proprietary C2 modem supporting 5G satellite connectivity.
Rising component and RAM costs are projected to push starting prices to $1,299 for the iPhone 18 Pro and $1,399 for the Pro Max.

title: Apple could debut two AirPods 5 models next month, per report - 9to5Mac

content:

AirPods 5 to feature regular and ANC variants
In a wide-ranging report published earlier tonight, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said Apple could announce a new Mac mini in the coming days, ahead of its expected September event.
Gurman also detailed several other products Apple has in the pipeline, including the AirPods 5, which could debut as early as next month. He says the company’s next event is expected to take place on September 9 and will also feature its first foldable iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro lineup, and new Apple Watches.
From the report:
The company is also preparing a range of new Apple Watches with minor changes, including upgrades to fitness tracking and a ceramic-case option for Series 12 models. And it’s planning to debut fresh AirPods as early as the September product launch event.
The rollout will include new AirPods 5, an update to Apple’s entry-level earbuds, the people said. That model was last refreshed in 2024. A camera-equipped version of the AirPods, meanwhile, isn’t expected until next year.
Interestingly, Gurman followed up on his own report with a post on X, adding that the AirPods 5 are expected to come in both regular and noise-cancellation variants:
While reporting on the AirPods 5 timeline has been scarce, the earbuds had generally been expected to arrive in 2027. Apple is also reportedly developing two camera-equipped AirPods models that will use Visual Intelligence and Siri for AI-powered features.

title: Galaxy S27 series design gets way more interesting in new leaked renders
author: Mihai Matei
content:
Last updated: August 24th, 2026 at 20:09 UTC+02:00
Still plenty of surprises left to uncover.
Asif Shaik - SamMobile
A few more design cues for the entire Galaxy S27 series have just been revealed through a series of fan-made CAD renders. According to leaks, next year's Galaxy S27 series might finally introduce a fourth main-series model and a new aesthetic for at least the Ultra.
In fact, apart from the redesigned camera housing, @UniverseIce says the Galaxy S27 Ultra will have almost the same overall dimensions as the S26 Ultra.
For reference, the latter measures 163.6 x 78.1 x 7.9mm and has a 6.9-inch display.
Ice Universe
Galaxy S27 Ultra CAD render
Moving on, beyond the redesigned camera housing, the Galaxy S27 Ultra will supposedly be relatively conservative in a couple of other key areas.
Namely, it apparently has the same S Pen holster and bottom speaker placement as the S26 Ultra — bottom-left.
Samsung has used this configuration for its Ultra models since the Galaxy Note 20 Ultra.
The rest of the upcoming S27 series does things a little differently, though. The source says the base S27, S27+, and S27 Pro have had the bottom speaker relocated from the left to the right side of the lower edge.
One render even shows an unusual S27 Pro design, and in a way, it's even more exciting than the Ultra. Let's check it out.
Disappointingly, some recent rumors suggest that the Galaxy S27 Pro will be more similar to the Plus than the Ultra. However, these new renders tell a different story, at least as far as the external design is concerned.
The one odd thing we noticed in these leaked renders is that the Galaxy S27 Pro also appears to have a brand-new camera housing design, similar to the S27 Ultra.
It looks wider but not quite as wide as the S27 Ultra's, nor as narrow as the usual vertical island beneath Samsung's camera rings.
Galaxy S27 Ultra CAD render, bottom
Galaxy S27 Pro CAD render, bottom
Galaxy S27 CAD render, bottom
Galaxy S27+ CAD render, bottom
This could be an error or a bad CAD, or more hopefully, it could be a hint that the Pro model, if it exists, may be a more compact replica of the Ultra. Samsung's Pro might be to the Ultra what the Apple iPhone 17 Pro is to the 17 Pro Max.
That may be too good to be true, though, and even if the S27 Pro has a new camera housing design, there's no guarantee the housing holds Ultra-grade camera hardware. For now, let's wait for more details before we draw any definitive conclusions based on this one CAD render.
Samsung should announce the Galaxy S27 series in early 2027, so there's plenty of time left to uncover its mysteries.
summary: Fan-made CAD renders have revealed new design cues for Samsung's upcoming Galaxy S27 series, including a potential fourth main-series model and a redesigned camera housing for the Ultra. The leaks indicate that while the S27 Ultra retains similar dimensions and layout to its predecessor, the base, S27+, and S27 Pro models feature relocated bottom speakers. Additionally, the Galaxy S27 Pro appears to feature a new camera housing design reminiscent of the Ultra, sparking speculation about its configuration.
key_points: The Galaxy S27 series may introduce a fourth main-series model and a new aesthetic for the Ultra.
The Galaxy S27 Ultra will feature nearly identical dimensions, S Pen holster, and bottom-left speaker placement as the S26 Ultra.
The base S27, S27+, and S27 Pro have their bottom speakers relocated from the left to the right side.
Leaked renders show the Galaxy S27 Pro with a brand-new camera housing design similar to the S27 Ultra.

title: The e-bike is the most complete expression of the bullying arrogance of cyclists
author: Stephen Bayley
content:
![Hundreds of Lime electric bicycles](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000494541930_17875910056820_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Hundreds of Lime electric bicycles](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000494541930_17875910056820_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
There are 75,000 e-bikes in London, and there are days when I get the impression that most of them have been brainlessly abandoned at the end of my road.
The concept of “dockless” e-bike carries – for some – a thrilling sense of care-free liberation, of being untethered from authority and practical constraints, of being unchained from the lunatic of regulations. A bicycling nirvana.
And that’s all true. But what it also means is that pedestrians have to pick their way through a tangle of wheels and handlebars, as if a Halford’s superstore has erupted on the street. Not every adopter of the exciting “dockless” concept, I have noticed, takes care to dock with social responsibility.
“Micro-mobility” means macro-inconvenience for the 10 million who are not of the 75,000. There are streets in central London where the pavement has wholly surrendered to the e-bike, as dangerous when stationary obstacles as they are when in motion and pedalled by a demented individual intent on maximising the value of the hire fee.
The wonder of it all is that no-one in authority seems to have anticipated the outcome. But we know in the matter of traffic management, TfL – and, indeed, provincial equivalents – conduct their business with a mixture of incompetence and malice.
A certain sign of systemic degeneration is chaotic transport. That’s where we are: the e-bike contributing generously to the anarchy of the roads.
Then there is the aesthetics, or what you might prefer to call terrible mess. Here the e-bike makes another significant contribution to the misery of the sensitive. There is nothing to be said, even ironically, for the benefits of clutter.
![Lime bikes lay in the road on March 27, 2024 in London, United Kingdom.](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000436252455_17875910469710_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqqVzuuqpFlyLIwiB6NTmJwfSVWeZ_vEN7c6bHu2jJnT8.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
People who care about urban housekeeping (and there are more than 75,000 of them) have for years been horrified by the visual pollution of overbearing, hectoring and redundant signage in our cities. Do this! Don’t do that! Smile, you’re on camera!
To the primeval forests of traffic-lights, poles and boards, sand-bags and cones can now be added the abandoned, static e-bikes making city life just that little bit more unpleasant for the majority.
But there is a general problem with bicycles of all kinds. God – or Nature – drives a hard bargain. In return for the beautiful and efficient theory of the bicycle which translates foot-power into smooth and silent propulsion, stabilised by benign gyroscopic forces, bicycles take up An Awful Lot of Space.
The problem of storage has not been solved, as hallways and verandas everywhere testify. Although a generation ago Brompton, manufacturers of the ingenious folding bike, offered an alternative to the clunky Borisbike: a system of elegantly designed deposit boxes to stow your compact machine neatly and politely.
This was too neat a solution for lazy authorities to consider. So Borisbikes were imported from Canada.
Untethered from authority means oblivious to traffic lights and innocent walkers. Total disdain for good manners. In this sense, the e-bike is the most complete expression of the cyclist’s arrogance.
In one generation, bicyclists have declined from being put-upon herbivores to becoming recklessly entitled, righteous, selfish bullies. E-bikes add dangerously high wattage to this forlorn caste.
summary: London's 75,000 dockless e-bikes have caused widespread street clutter, blocked pavements, and visual pollution for the city's pedestrians. The author argues that authorities failed to anticipate these problems, contributing to urban transport anarchy. Furthermore, irresponsible riders and the high volume of abandoned bikes reflect a growing sense of entitlement and arrogance among cyclists.
key_points: There are 75,000 e-bikes in London, often resulting in brainlessly abandoned vehicles on streets and pavements.
Dockless e-bikes create dangerous obstacles for pedestrians and cause severe visual clutter in urban areas.
Authorities, including Transport for London (TfL), are criticized for failing to manage or anticipate these transport issues.
Cyclists are characterized as having shifted from put-upon herbivores to recklessly entitled, selfish bullies amplified by e-bike wattage.

title: Warhammer 40k: A Legend Returns — New Space Marine Captain On Bike Revealed
author: Simon Berman
content:
Warhammer 40k: A Legend Returns — New Space Marine Captain On Bike Revealed
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wh40k-bike-header.jpg) 
A brand new kit is here for a venerable 40k hero. Get a closer look at the new Space Marine Captain!
It seems, unsurprisingly, that Codex: Space Marines may be near. We can tell from the roar of motors just over the horizon, heralding the return of a classic 40k character: the Space Marine Captain on Bike. Relegated to “Legends” status last edition, he’s back astride a new hog to join the recently revealed multi-part Outriders squad.
Revving Engines and Filling Gaps
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wh40k-marine-captain-bike.jpg)
He’s back, and he’s, err, he’s just fine. I’m not gonna lie, this is not the most exciting of models. If I was choosing a model to (presumably) kick off the lead-up to the release of the 11th edition Codex: Space Marines, I probably would have picked a model with a little more mustard on it. With that said, it’s a nice enough model and does fill one of very few gaps in the Space Marine model range.
Outriders have been a big part of the marine aesthetic since the early days of 40k. There’s just something charmingly ridiculous about a guy in power armor racing across the battlefield to decapitate an ork with a chainsword. It’s a nod to medieval knights on horseback and is an appealing part of all Marine chapters to one degree or another.
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wh40k-marine-bikes-photo.jpg)
Some chapters get more out of this kind of model than others. White Scars, Blood Angels, Dark Angels, and to some degree, Raven Guard all get good use out of the fast assault capabilities of an outrider squad. So, being able to attach a Captain to one unit and a Chaplain to another does offer some pretty mean, fast-moving melee support for any army. He does offer a bonus of Cleave 1 to his attached unit, which does add up to a pretty solid amount of attacks against horde armies like Tyranids or Orks.
At the end of the day, this is a “meat and potatoes” character option that’s nice to have back in the range, even if it’s not the most exciting model reveal of the year.
Astartes Chopper
Now, where this kit does get interesting is in its options. Like the upcoming Outriders kit, the bike itself has some limited posability. It can be built racing forwards or at rest with the bike tilted as the captain braces his foot and lines up a shot or gestures with his melee weapon.
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wh40k-marine-captain-bike-alts.jpg)
More excitingly, the kit includes a variety of weapon options. The Captain’s right hand can wield your choice of power sword, thunder hammer (it’s gonna be this one, isn’t it?), or plasma pistol. As a nice little bonus, if you choose the plasma pistol, the kit includes a sheathed sword for full WYSIWYG goodness.
The kit also includes a choice of five heads. Two helmeted and two bare; no matter the aesthetics of your chapter of choice, there’s a strong option here. I’m particularly fond of the one with a bionic eye, myself/
All in all, a necessary if not particularly sexy addition to Space Marine armies. It’s nice to see a model return from the oubliette of Legends status, though. I recently painted up a unit of outriders for my Blood Angels and found them fun models to paint, so there’s a non-zero chance I pick up another when the new kit arrives. With two squads of outriders, I suppose I might add a Captain and Chaplain to each. I’m kind of a sucker for extremely specialized detachments, so maybe something cool awaits in the codex?
Will we see bike-mounted librarians and apothecaries next?
![Simon Berman](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/avatar-simon-berman-300x300-1-150x150.jpg)
summary: Games Workshop has revealed a new Space Marine Captain on Bike kit for Warhammer 40k, signaling that a new Codex: Space Marines may be approaching. Although considered a conventional model that is not overly flashy, it successfully fills a previous gap in the miniature range. The new kit features multiple build options, including posable bike configurations, various weapon choices like a thunder hammer or power sword, and a selection of five heads.
key_points: A classic Space Marine Captain on Bike has returned from Legends status with a new kit.
The model provides fast-moving melee support and grants a Cleave 1 bonus to its attached unit.
The kit offers limited bike posability, allowing it to be built racing forward or at rest.
Players can choose from several weapon options including a power sword, thunder hammer, or plasma pistol.
The box includes a choice of five heads, consisting of helmeted and bare variants.

title: Protesting PS5 Players Now Plan Permanent Blackout, Meaning No GTA 6 or Wolverine
author: Push Square; Sammy Barker
content:
![Furious PS5 Players Unplug Their Consoles in Protest Against Sony 1](https://images.pushsquare.com/69d52814c6f59/furious-ps5-players-unplug-their-consoles-in-protest-against-sony-1.900x.jpg)
Update []:
Angry PS5 players now propose an “indefinite” boycott of Sony’s console, as the previously planned blackout steps up its intensity.
In updated language, protesters say the originally mentioned window of 23rd August through 30th August is now “a minimum requirement”.
“Everyone is encouraged to go indefinitely until Sony change course,” the Does It Play account, a leader in the protest, writes. “Pedal to the metal or we won't get anywhere!”
Major upcoming PS5 games include The Blood of Dawnwalker, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Marvel’s Wolverine, Control Resonant, and GTA 6 – among many others.
It’s going to be really interesting to see how resolute campaigners remain in the face of an increasingly strong release schedule.
Original Story: Irate PS5 players have started unplugging their consoles all around the world, as a protest against Sony gets underway.
The blackout – technically scheduled to start at 7pm local time, but already being observed by many participants – is designed to reduce the Japanese giant’s active users, a key performance metric for the company.
Campaigners suggest participants should keep their consoles unplugged from today through 30th August as a minimum. That means no logins, no gaming, and certainly no spending through the PS Store.
While the protest is primarily aimed at Sony’s decision to cease manufacturing physical discs in January 2028, organisers also argue that the company has grown “further apart from its fan base”.
Earlier this week, a Push Square poll concluded 92% of enthusiasts believe PS Studios would benefit from new management, after stories emerged it was rebooting development on spin-off game Horizon Hunters Gathering.
As of its most recent financial report, Sony attracted around 125 million monthly active users, an increase year-over-year. I think this number would have to drop precipitously to have any kind of effect.
Speaking with investors about potential boycotts and PS Plus cancellations, Sony’s CFO Lin Tao said it’s not seeing any “impact on our business”.
This organised and widely publicised blackout campaign may be protesters’ best opportunity to get the company’s attention, then. Will you be taking part?
summary: Furious PS5 players are participating in a blackout protest against Sony by unplugging their consoles and avoiding the platform. Originally scheduled for a single week, organizers are now calling for an indefinite boycott until Sony changes course. The protest is primarily driven by Sony's decision to cease physical disc manufacturing in January 2028, alongside broader concerns about the company's disconnect from its fanbase.
key_points: PS5 players are protesting against Sony by keeping their consoles unplugged.
The protest aims to reduce Sony's monthly active user numbers and prevent spending on the PS Store.
Organizers have escalated the action from a one-week blackout to an indefinite boycott.
The core grievance involves Sony's plan to stop manufacturing physical discs in January 2028.
Sony's CFO previously stated that the business has seen no impact from potential boycotts.
